researcher_notes: Coverage is genuinely uneven across the ~21 real POS vendors, which matches the vendor-first hypothesis: enterprise-scale vendors that actively press-release named restaurant wins (Toast, PAR Technology/Brink, NCR Voyix/Aloha, Oracle Simphony, Qu, Square for Restaurants, Revel Systems/Shift4) yielded solid dated records, several with explicit unit counts. SMB-oriented and hospitality-adjacent vendors (Clover, SpotOn, Heartland/Global Payments, TouchBistro, Talech, Rezku, Focus POS, Cake POS) rely on marketing language ('thousands of restaurants trust us') and vendor-page customer logos without dates or confirmable scope, so they came back thin as instructed rather than being padded with guesses. Two vendors on the approved list need a structural correction, not just thin evidence: (1) NewPOS is not a third-party company at all -- RB's own existing graph entity vendor-newpos documents it as McDonald's proprietary internal POS software (used only by McDonald's Corp), so it should not be researched or scored as an independent vendor; recommend Todd re-classify or drop it from the vendor universe. (2) Radiant Systems has not existed as an independent company since NCR Corporation acquired it in July 2011 for $1.2B; any current-day 'Radiant Systems' relationship claims would be stale by 15 years, and Radiant's Aloha-lineage assets now live inside NCR Voyix. A third correction worth flagging: Harbortouch is frequently conflated in secondary sources with sibling Shift4-owned POS brands POSitouch and Future POS -- a widely-repeated 2018 acquisition press release names Wendy's/Arby's/KFC/Dairy Queen/Denny's (Future POS) and Outback Steakhouse/Bonefish Grill/Houlihan's (POSitouch) as customers of those two brands specifically, NOT Harbortouch, and I did not carry that misattribution into the records below. Revel Systems was acquired by Shift4 Payments in 2024 (~$250M) and its customer-facing site now redirects to Shift4's food & beverage vertical page -- it is no longer an independently operated company, though the Revel product/brand name persists in at least one 2024 case study (Lazeez Shawarma) so I kept it as its own vendor line per the approved list. I also reused the 2026-07-21 research archive's candidate_evidence and verified_seed_evidence rows for the two vendors it had actually crawled (PAR and Qu -- the archive did not crawl Toast, NCR, Oracle, Square, or the smaller POS names), which is why PAR and Qu have the deepest, most confirmable bench of records. One data-quality note carried over from that archive: several PAR candidate rows tag 'Taco John's' and 'Pizza Ranch' to press releases that are actually about Papa John's and other unrelated PAR products (fuzzy brand-name matching artifacts) -- I did not include those false matches as PAR records. Separately, Pizza Ranch's Qu candidate-evidence rows may now be stale/superseded: Pizza Ranch announced a new exclusive NCR Voyix POS agreement in July 2026 with Aloha Next rollout starting 2027, which is the record I carried forward with high confidence; if Pizza Ranch previously ran on Qu, that relationship's current status is unconfirmed and should be treated as possibly superseded rather than active.

vendors_with_thin_or_no_evidence: Clover (Fiserv) -- vendor/press material cites aggregate scale ('nearly 200,000 restaurants worldwide,' new Clover Kiosk / Clover Reserve powered by Tabit / Clover Hospitality product launches) but no dated press release or case study naming a specific restaurant chain customer was found.

SpotOn -- extensive PR Newswire presence but entirely about G2/Capterra award rankings ('#1 Restaurant POS'); no named-brand case study with a confirmable date was found despite repeated targeted searches.

Heartland / Global Payments Restaurant POS -- found the Global Payments/Heartland $4.3B acquisition (completed April 25, 2016) and general product marketing, but no named restaurant chain customer press release or case study.
Xenial -- product appears to still be active in 2026 (recent Restaurant365 integration docs), but no named restaurant chain customer, case study, or press release was found.

TouchBistro -- La Bartola (single Toronto restaurant) and Bellwoods Brewery (single brewery) are the closest named examples; both are single independent locations, not chains, and neither has a clear publication date.

Agilysys (InfoGenesis) -- ticker AGYS; the vast majority of named, dated customer wins found (Marriott, Mandarin Oriental, IHG, SH Group, Wequassett Resort, Saratoga Casino & Raceway) are hotel/resort/casino groups adopting InfoGenesis for in-property F&B outlets, not standalone restaurant brands/chains. This may be a genuine category mismatch for a 'restaurant brand' evidence pass rather than a research gap -- worth Todd deciding whether hotel-embedded F&B counts for this graph.
Cake POS (Mad Mobile) -- only a marketing testimonial referencing Toastique was found, no press release or dated case study.
Talech (Mastercard) -- Pacino's Restaurant, Bar and Venue and Spitroast Kitchen are the only named examples, both small independent operations with no dates.

Rezku POS -- Andy & Friend's Coney Bar, Rico's Pizza, South Fork Grille, Chesapeake House Myrtle Beach are the named examples found; all single-location or very small independent operators, consistent with Rezku's apparent market focus, no dated press releases.
vendors_flagged_as_possibly_defunct_or_r: NewPOS -- not actually a third-party vendor. RB's own existing ecosystem_intelligence.json graph entity 'vendor-newpos' is explicitly documented as McDonald's proprietary internal POS software ('Not a third-party vendor deployment'), owned and operated by McDonald's Corp. It should not have been researched as an independent company and no third-party customer evidence exists or should be expected for it. Recommend removing it from the vendor universe or re-tagging it as brand-internal infrastructure rather than a vendor.

Radiant Systems -- acquired by NCR Corporation in July 2011 for approximately $1.2B (cash tender offer, $28.00/share); has not operated as an independent company for 15 years. Its hospitality POS lineage lives on inside NCR / NCR Voyix's Aloha product line today. No current, independent Radiant Systems customer relationships should be expected; any pre-2011 customer claims were not independently reverified in this research pass.
